In Class 9, during a cricket match, Mridul kept calling me names every time I missed a ball. "Butterfingers! Useless!" The others started laughing.
I felt my fists clench. I wanted to shout back.
Instead, I put down the bat and said, "I'm going home. I'm not fighting." Then I walked away.
Mridul shouted, "Coward!" But I kept walking.
At home, my hands were still shaking. But the next day, Mridul didn't say anything. Later he even said sorry.
Walking away felt like losing at first. But it was actually the smartest thing I did that year.
- Manoj

qa.a: Manoj said "I'm going home. I'm not fighting," which made it clear it was de-escalation, not running scared.

qa.q: How might Mridul have seen Manoj walking away?
qa.a: Mridul first called it cowardice, but later seemed to respect it, since he apologised.

Mother's note, Tuesday night
Tonight at dinner, Rafiq's father asked about his exam marks. Rafiq pushed his plate away and walked out of the room without a word.
His father got angry. "He's avoiding us."
I followed him to his room. He was sitting on the bed, head down.
I asked, "Do you need some time?"
He said, "I can't talk about it right now. Can we talk tomorrow?"
I told him that was fine, but next time, telling us "I'm stepping out, I'll be back" would help us understand.
I went back and told his father. Tomorrow we'll try again, calmly.
- Harsha

Monday
Today at the school gate Vikas wanted to talk about the fight we had last week, about the group project and who did more work. I just said, "Not now," and walked away fast toward the bus.
I saw his face. He looked hurt. I think he thought I didn't care or was avoiding him.
But I needed time. I was still upset, and I knew if I talked right then I'd say something mean.
Tonight I texted him: "Sorry I walked away. I just needed a break. Can we talk tomorrow after school?"
He replied, "Okay. Thanks for telling me."
I feel better now. Walking away without explaining makes it look like running.
- Tejas

qa.q: What did Tejas text Vikas?
qa.a: "Sorry I walked away. I just needed a break. Can we talk tomorrow after school?"

qa.a: Vikas likely felt hurt and rejected, thinking Tejas was avoiding him or didn't care.

qa.a: Tejas texted to explain the need for a break and promised to talk the next day.

qa.q: What would change if Tejas had not sent the text?
qa.a: Vikas might have kept believing Tejas was avoiding the friendship, and the trust between them could have worn down.

grounding: A teenager's diary shows walking away from a hard talk and then explaining it was a break, keeping trust.
